title: A projective coordinate complement is finite
statement: Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be integral Noetherian [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and let $Y\to S$ be projective [def-pc-projective-morphism]. Choose a finite affine open cover $Y_\alpha$ of $Y$ and closed $S$-immersions $Y_\alpha\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{m_\alpha}_S$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sbc-affine-space], with $m_\alpha\geq1$. Let $t_{\alpha r}:Y_\alpha\to\mathbf A^1_S$ be the restriction of the $r$th coordinate projection, and choose a dense open $V_{\alpha r}\subset\mathbf A^1_S$ for each coordinate. There is a nonempty principal open $S'=D(a)\subset S$ such that the reduced induced closed subscheme [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] of $Y\times_S S'$ on the complement of $\bigcup_{\alpha,r}t_{\alpha r}^{-1}(V_{\alpha r})$, restricted to $S'$, is finite over $S'$. Scheme and morphism conventions are those of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions].

proof.text: For each pair $(\alpha,r)$ put $C_{\alpha r}=\mathbf A^1_S\setminus V_{\alpha r}$. By the affine description of affine space this is a closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec}A[T]$. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] to $C_{\alpha r}$: it is $V(I_{\alpha r})$ for a radical ideal of $A[T]$. Since $A$ is a nonzero domain, $A[T]$ is a domain (the leading coefficient of a product of nonzero polynomials is the product of their nonzero leading coefficients). Thus $(0)$ is a prime and is the generic point of $\operatorname{Spec}A[T]$. A dense open contains this point: if it were in its closed complement, that complement would contain its closure, the whole spectrum. Consequently $I_{\alpha r}\not\subseteq(0)$; choose $0\ne P_{\alpha r}\in I_{\alpha r}$. If $C_{\alpha r}$ is empty one may choose $P_{\alpha r}=1$.

Let $c_{\alpha r}\ne0$ be the leading coefficient of $P_{\alpha r}$ and let $a=\prod_{\alpha,r}c_{\alpha r}$, with empty product $1$. The finite product is nonzero in the domain $A$, so $D(a)$ contains $(0)$ and is nonempty. Set $A'=A[1/a]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Each $c_{\alpha r}$ has inverse $(\prod_{(\beta,s)\ne(\alpha,r)}c_{\beta s})/a$ in $A'$. Replace $P_{\alpha r}$ by $Q_{\alpha r}=c_{\alpha r}^{-1}P_{\alpha r}\in A'[T]$, which is monic and still vanishes on the restricted closed complement. Restrict all charts and all opens to $S'=\operatorname{Spec}A'$. The restricted morphism $Y'\to S'$ is projective by [lem-pc-projective-base-change]. The ring $A'$ is Noetherian: every ideal $J$ of $A'$ equals the extension of its contraction to $A$, since $b/a^n\in J$ implies $b/1\in J$ and conversely; finite generators of the contraction generate $J$. Thus $S'$ is Noetherian.

The sets $t_{\alpha r}^{-1}(V_{\alpha r})$ are open in the affine open $Y'_\alpha$, hence in $Y'$, so their union $U$ is open. Use [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] on $T=Y'\setminus U$ to form $Z=T_{\mathrm{red}}$. On $Y'_\alpha=\operatorname{Spec}B_\alpha$ the same node describes $Z\cap Y'_\alpha$ as $\operatorname{Spec}(B_\alpha/J_\alpha)$, where $J_\alpha$ consists of functions vanishing in all residue fields at points of $T\cap Y'_\alpha$. Such a point lies outside every $t_{\alpha r}^{-1}(V_{\alpha r})$, so its $r$th coordinate lies in $C_{\alpha r}$ and $Q_{\alpha r}(t_{\alpha r})$ vanishes in its residue field. Hence $Q_{\alpha r}(t_{\alpha r})\in J_\alpha$ for every $r$. The closed chart embedding gives a surjection $A'[T_1,\ldots,T_{m_\alpha}]\twoheadrightarrow B_\alpha$; composing with the quotient by $J_\alpha$ therefore gives a surjection from
$$A'[T_1,\ldots,T_{m_\alpha}]/(Q_{\alpha1}(T_1),\ldots,Q_{\alpha m_\alpha}(T_{m_\alpha}))$$
onto $B_\alpha/J_\alpha$. This uses the statement's vanishing-ideal description, rather than assuming set-theoretic containment implies scheme-theoretic containment for a nonreduced source.

Write $d_{\alpha r}=\deg Q_{\alpha r}$. If one degree is zero, its monic polynomial is $1$ and $B_\alpha/J_\alpha=0$. Otherwise the equation $T_r^{d_{\alpha r}}=-\sum_{j<d_{\alpha r}}q_{\alpha rj}T_r^j$ reduces any monomial with exponent at least $d_{\alpha r}$ to a sum with strictly smaller total degree. Induction on total degree shows that the finitely many monomials $\prod_rT_r^{e_r}$ with $0\le e_r<d_{\alpha r}$ span the quotient algebra and its further quotient $B_\alpha/J_\alpha$ as $A'$-modules. For a geometric point $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S'$, the fibre of this affine chart is $\operatorname{Spec}((B_\alpha/J_\alpha)\otimes_{A'}\Omega)$; the images of the same spanning monomials span this algebra over $\Omega$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum] with $R=\Omega$ (a local ring with sole prime $(0)$): this fibre has finitely many points. The affine fibre description follows directly from the tensor-product universal property for a pushout of rings and the contravariant spectrum equivalence, and the spanning assertion uses only bilinearity of tensors. There is no assumption that this geometric fibre remains reduced.

The finitely many charts $Z\cap Y'_\alpha$ cover $Z$, and their inverse images cover each geometric fibre. Each has finite point set by the preceding step, so the point set of the whole fibre is finite. Also $Z\to S'$ is projective: compose its closed immersion into $Y'$ with the closed immersion $Y'\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_{S'}$ furnished by projectivity. The composite is a closed immersion, as can be checked on each affine target chart: successive surjections $R\twoheadrightarrow R/I\twoheadrightarrow(R/I)/\bar J$ are the single surjection $R\twoheadrightarrow R/J$. For every affine open $W\subset S'$, the inverse image $Y'_W$ is quasi-compact by projectivity of $Y'\to S'$. Its closed subset $Z_W$ is quasi-compact: extend each member of an open cover of $Z_W$ to an open of $Y'_W$, add $Y'_W\setminus Z_W$, and take a finite subcover of $Y'_W$; removing the complement gives a finite subcover of $Z_W$. Thus $Z\to S'$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. This verifies the quasi-compact H-projective convention of [def-pc-projective-morphism]. The target $S'$ is Noetherian by step 2 and every geometric fibre is finite by step 4. Thus [lem-fin-projective-finite-fibres] applies to $Z\to S'$ and gives the desired finiteness.
